text:
maya: Heads up — nightly perf alerts just flagged a regression in the runtime after today's merge. Release pipeline is paused until we root cause. :rotating_light:
perf-bot: nightly-perf /throughput: p50 increased 12%, p99 increased 35%, overall tokens/sec down ~18% (compare baseline 2026-03-17). Blocking release.
jiang: Ugh. Any obvious suspects from CI? Was there a kernel or batching change merged today?
tom: I saw PR #4123 land this morning — changed kernel selection heuristics to prefer fused-attn-kv-opt on long sequences. Also PR #4130 tweaked batching heuristics for small-latency requests.
manually: (not a participant)
anika: quick check — KV eviction rate spiked in prod-like perf runs. KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% to 67% on the perf harness. That would explain throughput loss.
maya: can someone bisect? Start with the merge window between commits: bc3a9f -> d9e7b11 (yesterday morning). If we can narrow to a commit we can revert/cherry-pick.
jiang: I'm on it. Starting git bisect locally against the perf harness.
jiang: git bisect start --bad d9e7b11 --good bc3a9f
jiang: git bisect run scripts/perf/check_throughput.sh --model=wide-16k --batch=8
ci-runner: running bisect jobs on ci/x86-heavy (10 agents). ETA ~18m.
tom: FYI, I noticed an accidental change in kernel selection table ordering in 7f4c3ea — it moved kv-priority above prefix-cache-sensitivity. Could cause more cache evictions if it routes to kernels that don't support prefix caching.
anika: That aligns. KV eviction increased when the runtime picked kv-optimized kernels that currently don't use the shared prefix store.
jiang: CI bisect finished: culprit commit is 7f4c3ea — PR #4123. Repro locally with the perf harness.
maya: OK. Patch plan: revert the ordering change in 7f4c3ea on main, cherry-pick into release branch v1.9.x, run nightly perf verification, then unpause rollout. Who can prepare the revert PR and verify?
sam: I'll open a revert PR and include both the fix and a unit test to prevent ordering regressions. PR #4142 created: revert(kernel-selection): restore prefix-cache preference — commit 8c9b2f4.
release-bot: Created release PR #4142 targeting main and backport workflow started for branch v1.9.x.
maya: good. @anika can you run the perf harness against the revert commit on the same CI pool and post the p50/p99 throughput? Please include KV hit-rate traces.
anika: starting perf run now. Command: ```./scripts/run_perf.sh --profile=nightly --commit=8c9b2f4 --model=wide-16k --batch=8 --duration=10m```
ci-runner: perf job queued: job/perm/1782102468-8c9b2f4. Using node pool gpu-highmem-rt.
anika: preliminary: p50 back down to within 2% of baseline, p99 within 5%, tokens/sec recovered ~16%. KV hit-rate is back to ~90%. Looks good.
maya: Excellent. Let's proceed with release branch backport and cherry-pick PR into v1.9.x, then run the release verification checklist.
sam: backport PR #4143 opened against v1.9.x. included changelog and test.
jiang: I'll coordinate verification of the cherry-pick. Running smoke + perf on staging.
jiang: smoke passed. Perf harness run complete: stable. Pushing for unpause.
maya: marking rollout blocker cleared. Will unpause canary in 10m after deploy-bot completes.
release-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: canary-2026-03-18T09:30Z (user: maya).
tom: postmortem note — follow-up: add kernel selection unit test & telemetry to ensure kernel choice doesn't disable prefix cache. Also update batching heuristics doc to include compatibility matrix.
anika: I'll open a follow-up PR to add telemetry and a perf regression alert that ties to KV hit-rate drops.
maya: Thanks all. Quick log of commands used for reproducibility:
```
# bisect
git bisect start --bad d9e7b11 --good bc3a9f
git bisect run scripts/perf/check_throughput.sh --model=wide-16k --batch=8

# revert
git revert 7f4c3ea -m 1
# cherry-pick to v1.9.x
git checkout v1.9.x
git cherry-pick 8c9b2f4
```
maya: Closing thread once canary is green. :white_check_mark:
